newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House leader Armey sees budget pact this year.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House leader Armey sees budget pact this year.

text.p: House Majority Leader Dick Armey said Thursday he expects to reach a balanced budget agreement this year with the Clinton administration.
"There will be a budget that will be passed in this Congress and it will be in this session, this year, and it will be signed into law," He said at a news conference.

Armey, a Texas Republican, said a budget resolution would likely be brought to the House floor for a vote in early May. A budget resolution essentially acts as a blueprint for the budget that later must be approved through a series of bills.
"I hope and I anticipate that that will be one where you will find a good deal of consensus" between the House, Senate, Republicans, Democrats and the White House, he said of the resolution.
Armey advocated being "patient" with the White House because of the large number of new people who have joined the administration after the election.

Armey said he recently had discussions with new White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles and believes he and the administration want to reach a balanced budget. "I believe he (Bowles) has a genuine honest resolve to get to a balanced budget, I think the White House has that," Armey said.
House Speaker Newt Gingrich, at the same news conference, said he believed the House would pass a balanced budget amendment to the U.S. Constitution. Such a measure failed recently in the Senate.
"I believe it will pass the House," Gingrich, a Georgia Republican, said, adding that he hoped ultimately the House version would pass the Senate.
